cli.network_sessions.next_page.role: Footer line of `lop network sessions` when a peer holds more rows than the page shown
cli.network_sessions.next_page.tone: factual and terse; a pointer to the next command, not a warning
cli.network_sessions.next_page.note: {peer} is a device name or ID, {shown} and {total} are row counts (ICU number arguments), {cursor} is an opaque paging token. Preserve all four verbatim, and keep `--peer` and `--cursor` exactly as written: they are command-line flags the reader types. No final period.

cli.network_sessions.paging_unsupported.role: Footer line of `lop network sessions` when a peer runs an older build that cannot page or search its listing
cli.network_sessions.paging_unsupported.tone: factual; say plainly that the listing is incomplete, without blaming the user
cli.network_sessions.paging_unsupported.note: {peer} is a device name or ID; preserve it verbatim. The rows shown (if any) are that device's capped default listing; a page or search could not be answered. No final period.

cli.network_sessions.relay_unpaged.role: Footer line of `lop network sessions --limit/--cursor/--query` when this device's own background relay is an older build that ignored the paging request
cli.network_sessions.relay_unpaged.tone: factual; state that the answer is not a page or a search, without blaming the user
cli.network_sessions.relay_unpaged.note: 'Relay' is the background mesh service on this device (glossary term). The rows shown, if any, are the older capped listing. No final period.
